title: REPORT on the implementation of the common security and defence policy – annual report 2025
part_text: 6. Underlines that in order to ensure effective deterrence against Russian aggression and sustainable peace in relation to Ukraine, credible and robust security guarantees must be offered, and coordinated collaboratively by all able and willing European and non-European partners; underscores that security guarantees should be established as Treaty obligations, guaranteeing an adequate response should Ukraine’s security be compromised, and complemented by measures to strengthen Ukraine’s own military deterrence; welcomes the conclusions of the meeting of the ‘Coalition of the Willing’ in Paris on 6 January 2026; strongly welcomes the proposal for a multinational ‘reassurance force’ for Ukraine, and encourages all EU Member States to thoroughly reflect on how they can best support such a force; welcomes the agreement to finalise politically and legally binding commitments to restore peace and security in the case of a future armed attack by Russia, and a clear framework for support to Ukraine, including sustaining its long-term military capabilities and deepened defence cooperation; regrets, however, that these security guarantees would only be implemented once a ceasefire is agreed upon, and that Vladimir Putin shows no willingness for such a ceasefire; notes the talks on a ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism; underlines the need to follow up on these ambitious proposals;
